items.title: Julius Handy Interview, 1973-05-09
items.q: Sylvester, he was on my daddy's bass. Well, we used to go out around the lakefront... we'd go up on their porch and we'd start playing.

ctx.x: I'll sit down now, since we got the thing moving. Okay, let's get your name now. Julius Handy. Yeah, and let's get your name, George. Evelyn Seville. Okay, and my name is Dick Allen.

What's today's date, hmm? Oh, I think the date is the 9th, isn't it? Am I wrong? Yes, it's May the 9th. May the 9th, 1973. Yeah, okay. And where are we? What's the address? Oh, yeah, 825 North Robinson. This is a resident Julius Handy. A brother of Captain John and Sylvester Henry. Oh, I see. While we're on that, you were talking about your father a little while ago and his farm. Yeah, my dad was great. He had a band for about 17 years. He had this fellow, Tom Albers. He has passed 635 to Gunders Street when he…
When you mention parade and second line, do you mean that they actually, um, followed behind him when he played?

items.title: Julius Handy Interview, 1973-05-09
items.q: they'd let me go to the dormitory with Sylvester and Sylvan

ctx.x: 12, so the boys were up in their teens.

Yeah, uh-huh, yeah. So when Sylvester was talking about, they were living in the dormitory. And sometimes they'd let me go to the dormitory with Sylvester and Sylvan, and most of the time I'd stay at the residence, you know, stay at their house. But it was amusing. Well, Dick, what did you play?
For me, just now? I just played blues.
